title: Operational Risk Cheat Cards for Sales
body:
Purpose:
- Fast-reference slide pack for AEs/SEs dealing with platform/ops risk objections when selling Redwood inference (hosted / dedicated / private).
- Focus: how to qualify risk quickly, recommend mitigations, and leave the customer with a concrete next-step (POC ask, runbook, SLA appendix).

How to use this pack (speaker notes):
- Slide 1: Quick intro — set expectations: we’ll map the customer’s operational worry to a pragmatic mitigation and a follow-up artifact (SLA, runbook, private deployment checklist). Keep it conversational: "What would keep you from shipping in 3 months?"
- Slides 2–7: Each slide is a one-card scenario. Read the scenario, rapid qualify questions, recommended Redwood levers, red flags, ask. Use as clipboard notes during calls.

Card A: "Bursty latency spikes in production"
- Scenario (one-liner): Customer sees intermittent latency spikes during peak windows, worried about user-facing timeouts.
- Rapid qualify questions:
  - When do spikes occur (time-of-day / campaign / cron jobs)?
  - 95/99 pct latency SLA target?
  - Are you currently using any prefix/KV caching or request-level caching?
  - Do bursts align with specific prompts or longer-sequence flows?
- Redwood levers to propose:
  - Dedicated capacity with autoscale baseline + burst policy (predictable headroom).
  - Smart routing: route to lower-capacity model variant during peaks (quantized or smaller model) with graceful degradation.
  - Enable prefix/KV caching for repeated context (reduce KV fetches).
  - Configure priority lanes / QoS for critical routes.
- Red flags to escalate to Solutions Eng:
  - Heavy long-seq requests (>2048 tokens) mixed with low-latency SLOs.
  - Customer expects sub-50ms at 90th for Llama2-70B-like workloads on shared pools.
- Ask: "Can we get a 72-hr trace + tail-latency sample?" (offer Redwood tracing hook and sample CSV)

Card B: "Data residency / audit and KMS concerns"
- Scenario: Regulated customer requiring logs to never leave EU and keys in their HSM.
- Qualify questions:
  - Which data classes must remain in-region? (PII, healthcare, payment tokens?)
  - Do they require customer-managed keys or HSM attestation?
  - Is offline/on-prem deployment acceptable?
- Redwood levers:
  - Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) + customer-managed KMS/HSM integration.
  - Audit log retention & export to customer SIEM (S3/ELK integration).
  - Network peering + strict egress rules and optional air-gapped install for enterprise.
- Red flags:
  - Requirement that human-in-the-loop logs be deleted within 24 hours globally (ask legal).
- Ask: "Schedule a compliance deep-dive with our Security Engineer and your SecOps — 60 minutes."

Card C: "Cost runaway from embeddings or high token churn"
- Scenario: ML team worried about sudden token cost increases from stray long prompts and embedding churn.
- Qualify:
  - Are embeddings deduplicated in your pipeline? Is vector store pruning configured?
  - Typical prompt length distribution? % of calls that exceed baseline?
  - Do you have caching at app layer?
- Redwood levers:
  - Suggest batching window and token-limited prompt templates, use Redwood Optimize recommendations for quantization and smaller embedding models.
  - Use prefix caching and response caching for repeated queries.
  - Cost monitoring alerts in Console: set token burn thresholds and automatic throttles.
- Red flags:
  - Third-party client sending raw user transcripts without truncation.
- Ask: "We’ll share a quick audit script (2 files) to sample token distribution from your logs"

Card D: "Model quality regression after rollout"
- Scenario: Team afraid a new model version will subtly change outputs and break UX.
- Qualify:
  - Do you currently run prompt-level regression tests or eval suites?
  - Are there gating thresholds for hallucinations / F1 / domain-specific metrics?
- Redwood levers:
  - Canary rollouts with automated metrics comparison (A/B) and automatic rollback rules.
  - Eval sets in Redwood Optimize: tie regression alerts to prompt sets and human review flows.
  - Pinning model versions per route; staged upgrade.
- Red flags:
  - No eval sets and heavy production reliance on deterministic outputs.
- Ask: "We’ll onboard one of your critical prompt templates into our eval harness and run a 7-day canary. Want to co-author the pass/fail thresholds?"

Card E: "Operational observability and debugging"
- Scenario: Platform/infra team wants end-to-end traceability for request tokens -> model inference -> cost attribution.
- Qualify:
  - Required retention window for traces? Who needs access?
  - Need token-level cost breakdown or just per-route?
- Redwood levers:
  - Console: token-level cost + latency breakdown, trace linking to request ids and S3 dumps.
  - Tracing hooks: span injection support for customer trace IDs.
  - Export connectors to Datadog/NewRelic/Splunk.
- Red flags:
  - Customer wanting raw model KV cache dumps or raw weights access.
- Ask: "Share a sample trace id and we’ll demonstrate Console trace + billing mapping in 30m."

Slide: Rapid objection-response snippets (soundbites)
- "We provide SLA-backed Dedicated capacity and automated fallback to smaller variants so you don’t hit catastrophic tail latency."
- "If residency or HSM is a blocker, our Private deployment + KMS/HSM integrations meet most enterprise compliance needs — let’s bring Security on the call."
- "We can run a 7-day canary with your eval set and auto-rollback rules; you’ll have concrete metrics before switching traffic."

Quick qualification checklist (one-liner pulls for call notes):
- SLA target? (p50/p95/p99)
- Typical sequence length / avg tokens
- Peak concurrency (RPS) and recent burst pattern
- Sensitive data classes? KMS/HSM needs?
- Who owns infra/SecOps on your side (name/email)?

Appendix: Example runbook bullet points to hand-off to Solutions/SE:
- Collect: 72-hr trace export (s3 path), token distribution CSV, sample failing prompts, expected SLO numbers.
- Initial workaround: route high-latency routes to dedicated pool; enable cache for top-20 routes; reduce model size for non-critical paths.
- Escalation: open INF-ops escalation ticket -> Solutions Eng pairing -> 1-week canary plan.

Open questions / TODOs in pack (internal):
- Need a short slide with pricing delta examples for Dedicated baseline + burst vs. hosted over 6 months (ask finance for numbers).
- Add a short script for the AE: "how to ask for trace exports without sounding intrusive".
- Get legal boilerplate for regional retention limits (EMEA / UK specifics).

Speaker note: keep cards short on calls. The goal is to move from vague fear to concrete next step (artifact + date). 

Contact & next steps (internal):
- If customer says "we need audit + HSM": book Security + Solutions (Priya Nair).
- If customer says "tail latency": route to SRE/Serving runtime (Diego Ruiz).
- If customer says "cost runaway": Solutions + Optimize (Ethan Brooks).

Revision history (temporary):
- 2025-11-18: initial sketch (Maya)
- 2025-11-25: added Card C (cost) and checklist (Priya)
- 2025-12-02: inserted runbook bullets + linked artifacts (Diego)

Notes-to-self:
- Convert to a 6-slide shareable PDF for SDRs (condense bullets to 2 lines per card).
- Consider an interactive Notion page where AE can copy pastable snippets per card.

End of doc.
